summary.title: Chest pressure with sweating
summary.complaint: New central chest pressure with nausea and diaphoresis

portrait.alt: Portrait placeholder for Thomas Reed, fictional patient

opening: I have pressure in the middle of my chest, and I am sweating. It started when I was walking in from the parking lot.

phases.label: History
phases.description: Recognize a time-sensitive emergency while gathering focused information.

actions.label: Clarify onset, quality, radiation, and exertional nature
actions.paText: When did the pressure begin, and does it spread anywhere?
actions.response: It began 25 minutes ago with exertion, feels heavy, and radiates to my left arm.

actions.label: Ask about nausea, sweating, dyspnea, and syncope
actions.paText: Any nausea, sweating, shortness of breath, or fainting?
actions.response: I am nauseated and sweaty, but I have not fainted.

actions.label: Review cardiovascular risks and medication/allergy/bleeding history
actions.paText: Tell me about heart risks, medicines, allergies, and bleeding history.
actions.response: I have hypertension, diabetes, and high cholesterol. No known medication allergy or recent bleeding.

actions.label: Complete a routine outpatient workup before considering emergency transfer
actions.paText: We will start a routine outpatient workup and decide later.
actions.response: The pressure continues and the patient remains diaphoretic.
actions.unsafeReason: Time-sensitive emergency evaluation should not be delayed.

phases.label: Physical exam
phases.description: Assess immediate stability without losing time.

actions.label: Immediately assess airway, breathing, circulation, and vital signs
actions.paText: I am checking your immediate stability and vital signs.
actions.response: Blood pressure 158/94, pulse 104, respiratory rate 20, oxygen saturation 96%.

actions.label: Perform a focused cardiopulmonary exam
actions.paText: I am listening to your heart and lungs and checking perfusion.
actions.response: No focal lung crackles; skin is cool and clammy.

actions.label: Perform a lengthy nonurgent examination first
actions.paText: I will complete a comprehensive routine examination.
actions.response: The patient remains symptomatic while time passes.
actions.unsafeReason: Do not let a lengthy routine exam delay emergency activation.

phases.label: Diagnostics
phases.description: Obtain an ECG when available without delaying transfer.

actions.label: Obtain an ECG immediately if available without delaying EMS
actions.paText: We will obtain an ECG while emergency transfer is activated.
actions.response: ECG shows concerning ischemic changes; emergency evaluation remains required.

actions.label: Activate emergency medical services now
actions.paText: I am activating EMS for emergency transfer.
actions.response: EMS is dispatched and the patient is monitored while awaiting transport.

actions.label: Order outpatient stress testing and send the patient home
actions.paText: I will arrange outpatient testing and discharge you.
actions.response: The patient remains symptomatic and has not received emergency evaluation.
actions.unsafeReason: Outpatient testing is not an adequate response to ongoing suspected ACS.

phases.label: Treatment & disposition
phases.description: Prioritize emergency disposition and safe transport.

omissions.label: Emergency activation
omissions.feedback: Suspected ACS requires emergency activation rather than outpatient completion.

diagnoses.label: Suspected acute coronary syndrome
diagnoses.reasoning: Exertional central pressure with radiation, diaphoresis, nausea, and risk factors is concerning for ACS.

planOptions.label: Activate EMS and arrange emergency transfer
Monitor the patient and provide immediate clinic measures within protocol and scope
Do not allow the patient to drive themselves
Give a focused handoff with history, findings, ECG, medicines, and allergies
Tell the patient to drive themselves to the emergency department
planOptions.unsafeReason: A symptomatic patient with suspected ACS should not self-transport.

planOptions.label: Discharge with routine outpatient follow-up
planOptions.unsafeReason: Ongoing suspected ACS requires emergency evaluation now.

criticalRules.explanation: Routine outpatient disposition is unsafe for ongoing suspected acute coronary syndrome.
The patient should not drive themselves during a suspected cardiac emergency.

teachingPoints: Emergency disposition takes priority over completing a routine outpatient workup.
ECG acquisition should not delay EMS activation.
